# Charter — T4 Kanban coach (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

- **Project:** T4 'Kanban coach', track v2, ADM phase G, plateau capability, tranche 4, project `01a1d039-0d33-7e7e-890e-b437b0c78db9`, plan `docs/SPEC_V2.md#12` (draft). The row is `status: active` with `meta.measured_status: built`, `meta.viability: rework`, `meta.depends_on: [T3, P0]`, `meta.issues: [75]` (issue #75 'T4 — Kanban coach', closed), `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]` and `meta.closure_outputs: [closure-review]`. It was reopened at 2026-11-24T16:57:39Z for 'the retrospective MSP/TOGAF/SAFe rework of tranche 4 (#526)' under decision `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`, and tranche 4 was authorised at 2026-11-24T17:04:34Z by review `01a20e84-325b-7fef-8f40-50b5e53550e9`.
- **Mandate:** SPEC_V2 §12 defines T4 as the kanban coach: an injected failure yields exactly one coach card and one remedy; a repeat signature escalates; no coach card about a coach card; a systemic class opens a kata. The retrospective reconstitutes the MSP/TOGAF lifecycle record for that capability — charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review and the two expected outputs, project-brief and evidence.
- **Scope:** `coach_interruption` and the append-only `coach_remedy`; the closed triage set (transient, conveyor_defect, job_defect, project_decision, external) and the closed remedy set (retry, move, repull, block, ask, note); the `coach.window` policy (24-hour default window, 0.7 confidence floor, `conveyor_defect` as the default systemic class, kata pin); the human gates `coach.escalation`, `coach.ask` and `coach.kata`; `kata.open` as the systemic-learning hand-off; the executable gate `scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py` and the twelve tests in `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs`.
- **What this retrospective does NOT attest:** it does not attest a green run of the coach gate at this snapshot, a waiver of the red findings in `docs/evidence/rework/T4.json`, the tranche-4 exit criteria, or closure. At the snapshot the charter check fails on the missing `CONVEYOR_SSH_KEY` transport, the live delivery contract's review `01a2028e-a1be-779d-a762-8d118fc2ec0b` records level `non_conformant` without a published `delegation_ref`, fifteen mandatory artefact packages remain open and the P1 rework package `std-togaf-phase-g-t4-g:T4` is unresolved. The project stays active; no closure review is reissued here.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T4 Kanban coach (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

body.assignment: Rework T4 by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and publish the project-brief and evidence outputs that SPEC_V2 §12's kanban coach owes. The work records the non-conformant review inherited from the facts, leaves the project active, and claims no closure.
body.scope: The coach write path on the board and the action spine: `coach_interruption` and `coach_remedy`, the five-term triage set and six-term remedy set, the `coach.window` policy (default 24-hour window, 0.7 confidence floor, systemic classes), the human gates `coach.escalation`, `coach.ask` and `coach.kata`, the `kata.open` hand-off for systemic classes, and the executable gate `scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py` over the twelve tests in `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs`. Out of scope: the kata lifecycle after open (T5, issue #77), the board UI (S12), card writes outside the action path, and any second board or comment store.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect (conveyor-e2e) authors the pack; the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board) approves the Phase A–D set; conveyor-approver records the Phase-G review. The approver `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`, distinct from the requester `01a1e607-17d9-77d3-98d3-a43a87c4633d`, approves the contracts and took the scope baseline `01a2028d-e17b-793d-9ea2-fe4f7f8e2b72` on 2026-11-22T09:19:40Z.
body.acceptance_criteria: SPEC_V2 §12's four clauses, each bound to named tests by `scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py`: (1) an injected failure yields exactly one coach card and one remedy — `an_interruption_yields_one_coach_card_one_triage_and_one_remedy`, `the_seeded_coach_process_yields_one_card_one_triage_and_one_remedy`, `a_duplicate_remedy_is_refused`; (2) a repeat signature escalates — `a_repeat_signature_escalates_instead_of_a_second_card`, `an_escalated_signature_is_not_retried`; (3) no coach card about a coach card — `a_failed_coach_run_never_opens_a_coach_card`, `a_nested_coach_run_is_refused`, `a_coach_card_cannot_be_created_through_the_public_path`, `the_coach_chain_settles_at_one_card`; (4) a systemic class opens a kata — `a_systemic_class_opens_one_measured_kata`, `a_systemic_class_without_a_pinned_instrument_escalates`, `a_transient_class_opens_no_kata`. The acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T4.toml`; the snapshot records no green run of these clauses, so this statement does not record acceptance.
body.contract: This statement `01a2028b-dde6-7ed4-9e47-6e582f2341d8` sits on the approved scope baseline `01a2028d-e17b-793d-9ea2-fe4f7f8e2b72` and is complemented by the delivery contract `01a2028d-942b-759a-ad59-ab9c38629977` (board decision `01a2028d-abf9-78fb-a9c6-eb06c4bdd634`), under the statement's own approval `01a2028b-f63c-7c27-b580-d4cba2c1e70f`. Both contracts are retrospective instruments under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`; they bind the rework to its capacity, acceptance and evidence terms and expressly withhold closure.

## Entries

Nine stakeholders on the influence/interest/engagement axes. The sponsoring group decides the tranche and the exit criteria; the SRO is accountable; the programme architect is responsible for the slice and the pack; the Architecture Board approves the set and the contract. conveyor-approver supplies the live non_conformant review that this retrospective carries forward rather than overwrites. Board users and runtime operators consume the one-card rule and the coach.window policy; the T5 kata owners receive systemic-class katas; the coach agent is told, by its allowed_actions, that it diagnoses but never chooses the remedy.

## Links

Derives from SPEC_V2 §12's T4 row and the delivery plan's dependency line (T4 after T3), the coach policy in `crates/actions/src/coach.rs` and the kata hand-off in `crates/actions/src/kata.rs`. # Requirements Catalog — T4 Kanban coach (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase A; plateau psa; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d33-7e7e-890e-b437b0c78db9; artefact 01a2028c-94d6-7e50-9d94-9e94feda14aa; retrospective under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Ten requirements. R1–R6 restate SPEC_V2 §12 in testable form and bind each clause to its named test in `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs`. R7 keeps the remedy honest: the effect runs before the row and a failure rolls both back. R8 makes the confidence floor explicit (0.7, ask below it). R9 requires the gate to be an instrument, not a prose claim, and binds its evidence to the checked-out HEAD. R10 protects the audit trail by grant rather than convention.

## Links

Derives from SPEC_V2 §12 and §6.2, the module documentation in `crates/actions/src/coach.rs`, the kata open gate in `crates/actions/src/kata.rs`, and the gate instrument `scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py`. Realizes the Phase A requirements view for the coach capability.

## Document

The catalogue states what must hold. It does not state that it held at the snapshot: the executable mapping exists and names twelve tests, but no sha-bound run is present in the inputs, and the project acceptance record is red on governance checks.

# Data Entity/Data Component Catalog — T4 Kanban coach (Phase C)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase C; plateau hld; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d33-7e7e-890e-b437b0c78db9; artefact 01a2028d-27ab-7464-918c-e0e07c1a43dc; retrospective under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Nine entities and components. The pair coach_interruption/coach_remedy is deliberately asymmetric: the interruption must change as triage and state advance, while the remedy is append-only and the runtime's grants forbid editing it. The partial unique index is the structural guarantee behind 'one card per signature'. The policy row is data, not code: operators can widen the window, move the confidence floor or declare additional systemic classes without a deploy. The kata and its measurement are referenced here because the coach opens them; their full lifecycle is T5's.

## Links

Derives from the coach store contract in `crates/store/src/coach.rs`, the policy read in `crates/actions/src/coach.rs`, the kata open path in `crates/actions/src/kata.rs`, and the grants in `scripts/grants-runtime.sql`. Realizes the Phase C data view for the coach capability.

## Document

The catalog describes the entities as the code and migrations define them. It does not assert that every migration ran in production at the snapshot, nor that the measurement path has been exercised; those claims belong to a green gate run that the inputs do not contain.

value.usage: coach_remedy receives no UPDATE or DELETE grant for the runtime role in scripts/grants-runtime.sql; a correction is a new interruption, never an edit

entries.axis_b: apply, then record, or roll back

value.usage: the remedy's effect runs in the same transaction before the coach_remedy row; a failed effect rolls the remedy back so an interruption is never remedied by a write alone

# Technology Standards Catalog — T4 Kanban coach (Phase D)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase D; plateau hld; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d33-7e7e-890e-b437b0c78db9; artefact 01a2028d-57ed-7267-ab06-1a3585f3acd8; retrospective under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Nine standards. The database is deliberately simple: two coach tables, one partial unique index, closed text columns with CHECK backstops. The interesting guarantees are in process, not schema: the runtime cannot edit a remedy, the model cannot choose one, the effect precedes the row, and the policy row rather than a deploy controls the window, the floor and the systemic set. The gate instrument is a standard in its own right: a clause that no named test proves is a gate failure, and evidence that does not hash to the current HEAD is stale by construction.

## Links

Derives from SPEC_V2 §6.2, §6.3, §9.3–§9.4 and §12, the coach and kata modules, the store contract and grants, and the gate instrument. Realizes the Phase D standards view for the coach capability; reuses the repository's action-registry and RLS conventions.

## Document

The catalog records the standards the code embodies. It does not record a successful enforcement run: the compile and test verdict belongs to CI, and at this snapshot the project acceptance record is red on the governance checks enumerated in the evidence output.

body.capacity: T4 delivers the kanban coach as one write path over the board and the action spine. coach.interrupt opens exactly one coach card and one coach_interruption row keyed by (tenant, card, signature); coach.triage records one class from the closed five-term triage set; coach.remedy applies at most one class from the closed six-term remedy set (retry, move, repull, block, ask, note). The window is the coach.window policy (24 hours by default), the confidence floor is 0.7 (below it the remedy is ask and the coach.ask gate opens the ask_fr process), and a repeat signature inside the window is handled by coach.escalation rather than a second card. A systemic class (conveyor_defect by default) opens one measured kata through kata.open; the kata lifecycle after open belongs to T5 (issue #77).
body.acceptance: SPEC_V2 §12's gate, executable in scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py and proved by the twelve tests in crates/actions/tests/coach.rs: one interruption yields one coach card, one triage and one remedy; a repeat signature escalates and an escalated signature is not retried; no coach card about a coach card, because a failed coach run never opens one, a nested run is refused, the public card path refuses card_type coach, and the chain settles at one card; a systemic class opens one measured kata, a systemic class without a pinned instrument escalates, and a transient class opens no kata. The manifest is acceptance/programme/T4.toml. The gate is red at the 2026-11-24 snapshot, so this contract records the acceptance terms and does not certify them.
body.evidence: The evidence route is docs/evidence/rework/T4.json (the 2026-11-24 project acceptance run at 2026-11-24T21:07:28Z), docs/evidence/rework/T4-coach-gate.json (the sha-bound run file the instrument writes), the twelve named tests in crates/actions/tests/coach.rs, and the published evidence output 01a1f2c9-b705-7665-b4e9-1b0ea03e5c95. The existing project-brief publication is 01a2028e-0490-74e9-8334-3deb68d10593 (2026-11-22T09:19:58Z); the retrospective's change record is 01a20e7e-bf2d-71ae-aecb-bcbdb45e733f. The snapshot contains no green coach-gate run, and this contract claims none.

wbs_deliverable.title: The kanban coach — one interruption, one coach card, one triage and at most one remedy, with escalation, a recursion cap and a measured kata for systemic classes

review.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review carries the level non_conformant recorded by the facts: the delivery contract 01a2028d-942b-759a-ad59-ab9c38629977 was reviewed on 2026-11-22T09:20:30Z by conveyor-approver as review 01a2028e-a1be-779d-a762-8d118fc2ec0b, and no active waiver exists (the acceptance run reports zero waivers). The project acceptance record docs/evidence/rework/T4.json, generated 2026-11-24T21:07:28Z, is red: T4-charter fails because the charter check cannot reach the transport (CONVEYOR_SSH_KEY is not set in the run environment) rather than because the project lacks a charter asset; T4-review fails because the live contract's review has no published delegation_ref or sits at non_conformant without a waiver; T4-artefact-standard lists fifteen mandatory artefact packages open; T4-rework names the unresolved P1 package std-togaf-phase-g-t4-g:T4; and the manifest gate aggregates those four failures. What passes is real and worth stating: the scope baseline 01a2028d-e17b-793d-9ea2-fe4f7f8e2b72 is approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545; the live delivery contract is board-approved by 01a2028d-abf9-78fb-a9c6-eb06c4bdd634; the closure gate 01a20e7e-c3b7-79ac-b2b0-dcc6e1e595c0 was decided by an approver distinct from its requester; PI cadence 01a202a1-dbb9-7e49-b64a-cf97c3fab095, PI plan and PI objectives are published; the WSJF inputs and the demo credit are present; the tranche-4 lesson 01a20e7e-6ede-7f85-97a8-e857b4b0e187 carries evidence; and no P0 product finding is open. The coach gate itself is not a blocker at this level: scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py binds each SPEC_V2 §12 clause to named tests in crates/actions/tests/coach.rs and can sha-bind a run, but the snapshot contains no such run, so the review neither asserts nor assumes a pass. # Project brief — T4 Kanban coach (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

## Outcome

T4 is the kanban coach of the conveyor: an injected failure becomes exactly one coach card, one triage from a closed five-term set, and at most one remedy from a closed six-term set. A repeat signature inside the coach.window escalates through coach.escalation instead of opening a second card; a failed coach run never opens a coach card, so the coach chain settles at one card; and a systemic class opens one measured kata while a transient class opens none. The record claims the slice built (`meta.measured_status: built`) and issue #75 is closed, but the 2026-11-24 acceptance run is red on governance checks and this retrospective does not upgrade the claim to accepted.

## Boundary

Out of scope: the kata lifecycle after open — observe, analyse, hypothesise, propose, measure, adopt — which belongs to T5 (issue #77); the board UI, which belongs to S12; card writes outside the action registry; and any second board, comment or membership store. The coach opens a kata but never adopts one: adoption is a human decision carrying evals:approve.

## Reuse sources

The board card, the process run and the approval primitive from P0; the failed-run provenance from T3, on which the dependency line places T4; the action registry and its HTTP/MCP parity; the policy ladder, reused for coach.window; and the kata action family in `crates/actions/src/kata.rs`, which supplies the systemic-learning hand-off. The gate instrument reuses the repository's evidence convention: a sha-bound JSON run under `docs/evidence/rework/`.

## Inception units

This retrospective is the inception record. It carries the charter, the Statement of Architecture Work 01a2028b-dde6-7ed4-9e47-6e582f2341d8, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts 01a2028c-33a0-76d6-acd6-57365a79dd10, 01a2028c-6415-7dbb-bb08-ef2baa58aaa4, 01a2028c-94d6-7e50-9d94-9e94feda14aa, 01a2028c-c575-749c-a0c8-82c44effa477, 01a2028c-f584-75ea-90cd-b929dd945aa4, 01a2028d-27ab-7464-918c-e0e07c1a43dc and 01a2028d-57ed-7267-ab06-1a3585f3acd8, the delivery contract 01a2028d-942b-759a-ad59-ab9c38629977 and the one WBS deliverable whose WSJF inputs are 10, 8, 9 and 13.

## Dependencies

T4 depends on T3 for the failed-run provenance that supplies the interruption signature, and on P0 for the board card, the process spine, the action registry and the approval primitive. It hands systemic classes to T5. Governance dependencies are the approved scope baseline 01a2028d-e17b-793d-9ea2-fe4f7f8e2b72, the tranche-4 authorisation 01a20e84-325b-7fef-8f40-50b5e53550e9 and the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Acceptance

SPEC_V2 §12's four clauses, bound to twelve named tests by `scripts/check-t4-coach-gate.py`: one card, one triage and one remedy per interruption; repeat escalation without retry; no coach card about a coach card; and one measured kata for a systemic class, with escalation when no instrument is pinned and no kata for a transient class. The acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T4.toml`. At the snapshot the gate is red: `docs/evidence/rework/T4.json` fails the charter check on the missing transport, the review on its delegation reference, the artefact standard on fifteen open packages and the rework check on the P1 package `std-togaf-phase-g-t4-g:T4`.

## Capabilities

Eight capabilities: interruption capture, closed triage, remedy execution, repeat-signature escalation, recursion containment, systemic learning through one measured kata, human decision gates for escalation, ask and adoption, and conformance evidence through the sha-bound gate instrument. Each is declared built with a named code or test carrier; none is recorded as accepted at this snapshot.

## Plan

The retrospective proceeds in the order the rework runner applies: publish the charter and Statement of Architecture Work, create the seven A–D artefacts with their exact titles, record the delivery contract and the WBS deliverable, record the Phase-G review at non_conformant, and publish this brief and the evidence output. It then stops. It does not reissue the closure review 01a20e7d-f065-758b-98b8-3878a95c7314, does not take a closure gate, and leaves the project active so the live governance failures can be fixed and the coach gate run under the repository's CI route.

# Evidence — T4 Kanban coach (retrospective, 2026-11-24)
